description: Splices analysis files end to end in the frequency domain: the output .ana plays infile1 followed by infile2 (verified by resynthesis: 2.023 s + 1.521 s -> 3.547 s, +0.08% frame padding). Takes NO parameters. The CDP usage is variadic ('analjoin join infile1 infile2 [infile3 ....] outfile' - a 3-input join verified, durations sum); this entry pins the 2-input form, reach for execute() to join more at once or chain joins. Because the join happens between spectral frames, the seam avoids the time-domain click/splice problem - transitions inherit the phase-vocoder's smoothness. All inputs must share analysis parameters ('Incompatible analysis-sample-rate' refusal otherwise). Deterministic.
musical_use: The spectral-domain splice: concatenate materials WITHOUT leaving the analysis domain, so a whole chain (anal -> transform -> join -> more transforms -> synth) stays lossless between stages. Musically it shines for building composite sources for further spectral processing - join a vowel to a bowed note to a gong, then blur/stretch/morph the composite as one object so the processing rides across the seam and glues the identities together. Also the natural way to extend material before time-domain-hostile spectral ops, or to assemble A-B pairs for morph morph/bridge experiments from one continuous file. The seam itself is smoother than a plain waveform butt-splice but is NOT a crossfade - for a gradual transition use morph bridge/morph instead, or overlap-and-mix after resynthesis.

examples.description: Concatenate two analysis files into one continuous spectral object.
examples.expected_use: Output .ana = input1 then input2; duration is the sum (+<0.1% frame padding). Feed .wav sources and auto-PVOC converts both with matching settings.

known_issues: Inputs must share analysis parameters: a -c2048 .ana against a default one refuses 'ERROR: INVALID DATA / ERROR: Incompatible analysis-sample-rate in input file ...'. The engine's auto-PVOC uses consistent defaults, so wav-fed chains are safe; pre-converted .ana files from other settings are the risk case.
Variadic upstream: 3+ input files are accepted by the binary (3-input join verified, outdur = sum of all three) but this entry pins input_arity 2; use execute() or chained joins for more.
A single input refuses with 'Insufficient input files for this process'; time-domain input refuses with 'File ... is not of correct type'.
Deterministic: two runs 1.2 s apart identical in the .ana data chunk (compare data chunks, not raw bytes - the RIFF date chunk differs).

Duration expression uses indur1 + indur2; for .ana inputs whose source durations aren't reachable in the graph the pre-flight skips (standard spectral-chain behavior) and the watchdog covers runaways.
